steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Mix butter, garlic powder, paprika, and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper in a small bowl; set aside.
Slice the bottom off bok choy; remove and clean stalks. Sprinkle seasoned salt and remaining 1 teaspoon black pepper over both sides of stalks.

Place bok choy on the preheated grill. Brush with seasoned butter mixture, close the grill top, and cook until stalks show grill marks and leaves are crisp at the edges, 3 to 4 minutes. Turn bok choy, brush with butter mixture, close the top, and cook other sides, 3 to 4 more minutes. Brush with any remaining butter mixture and transfer to a platter to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Bok Choy
raw_recipe.description: Grilled bok choy is brushed with seasoned butter as it cooks, leaving grill marks on the tender stems and crispy leaf edges. A delicious summer side!

review.reviewBody: I only had baby bok choy, but tried to make the dish anyway. I cooked it for far less time, basically just enough time to get them on the grill, butter them, flip them over, butter them, then cook for a little bit. Some of the leaves did get a little burnt, but it was still amazingly delicious!

Very good. Made the vinaigrette/spices in a quart mason jar. Used baby bok choy, left whole. Put 2 at a time in the mason jar with lid & shook to get oil & spices distributed. To cook evenly I grilled the whole baby bok choy with the stem in direct hot fire and the leaves in the indirect fire. The charred parts were most tasty. Next time I'll slice the baby bok choy in half to get more char.

Because of the pouring rain tonight, I grilled this on my indoor grill. I also blanched the bok choy for just a minute or two first in salted boiling water. I used 1 1/2tblspns of olive oil instead of 1/4c of butter (I wanted to keep the fat content way down), kept the spices the same except the season salt which I used half of, and just 1/8tsp of fresh black pepper. Submitter has it down twice so I used the lesser. Thought
1tspn was extreme. Added red hot pepper flakes to mine. I enjoyed this! Might be better with baby bok choy since it may be more tender. Looking forward to making again and grilling outside for a more smokey taste.

I chopped all of the Bok Choy and put in a ziploc bag with all of the ingredients. I also added some mushrooms. I let this marinate for about an hour and then put in on the grill in a grill basket. The texture was great, just seemed to be lacking in flavor. Next time I will add a little heat.

My husband and I thought this was pretty good. I used baby bok choy and olive oil instead of butter... mixed the basting ingredients in a bowl, prepared the bok choy leaves, added them to the bowl, and massaged the oil throughout the leaves. I put the leaves directly on the grill. The ends of the leaves came out crunchy and a little burnt, the stalks were warm and tender. There were some bitterness, probably from the burnt pieces, but not all of the burnt parts were bitter. It was good, and I'll probably make it again. Thanks for sharing!

Just the change I was looking for from sautéing this veggie. I found the basting brush difficult to use on the leaves while grilling so I just put it all in a covered bowl with the ingredients and shook it around. Worked great and less work. Served with hamburgers and hot dogs. Yum!

Holy Bok Choy! I prepared this according to the recipe except I added 1 Tbsp. of balsamic oil to the melted butter - then finished it off with a little grated parmigiano right after I removed it from the grill. Delicious!

We found that the bok choy burned on the grill before the stalks became tender enough to eat. Our grill is older and hard to perfectly control temp, but on med-high we had charred leaves and tough stems. Best to start on lower part of grill and finish on upper racks. I ended up pan-searing the bok choy because I could get a bit of char but then cover it to finish cooking it through.

My hubby LOVED this and he rarely will eat veggies. SO nice to have another veggie to make. Made it two ways, used olive oil for half and butter for the other half. Both were great. Followed suggestion to put all in a bowl and coat the leaves first. Saves me basting in the dark. Definitely will make again.

Being the first time I have ever eaten bok choy, I made the recipe exactly. I found it to be incredibly salty, and we had nearly a tablespoon of the seasoning mix left over. Saltier than dried seaweed, but next time I will cut the salt back by half and try again as it had potential.
I could not believe how good this was! I put the bok choy into a grilling basket and kept stirring and basting it with the seasoned butter as it grilled. It took up less room on the grill that way
Easy to adapt, good baste! Nice to switch it up from grilled endives. Will definitely make this one again.
Tried it today.. Delicious

Super delicious! I never knew what to do with the bok choy that came in my CSA box. I came across this recipe & it's one of my favorites. The leaves are like addicting potato chips - you can't eat just one! The only caveat is that you need to eat them right away. If you try to keep them "warm," they will just get soggy. I seldom make the entire amount of bok choy & usually cut the butter recipe in half. So yummy.
Perfect on the grill with hamburgers. everyone was impressed. Will definitely make this again!
So quick and easy. I was able to grill it after I took the meat off the grill. Flavor and texture was great.
We liked the flavor of the leaves the best. A few leaves got a little charred. You have to keep an eye on your grill while cooking!
I forgot to add the butter ... It wasn't necessary great taste.

I rather liked bok choy grilled.. It brings out a whole new flavour. I had 12 baby bok choys and felt that the amount of butter would be too much, so I used only 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 tablespoon of avocado oil. I kept everything the same with the exception of the extra pepper. 
Will definitely grill bok choy again but will play with flavours. 
Thanks for the idea
Love it!
